title: Regular City Council Meeting 08/04/26
caveat: Findings from an automated review of an auto-captioned recording. Verify specifics against the video before repeating them.

findings.meeting_summary: The Mattoon City Council addressed several municipal matters including public comments on animal ordinances and neighborhood flooding, city personnel positions, property acquisition, and infrastructure grant funding. Key approvals included equipment replacement at the water treatment plant and authorization to solicit bids for Phase 1 of the Little Wabash Drainage Project.

topics.what_happened: The council considered approving a $74,868 proposal from Hydro-Kinetics to replace 25-year-old modulating electric actuators on Filter #2 at the water treatment plant. City staff explained that replacing these five actuators maintains equipment consistency across all plant filters and ensures ease of maintenance.

The council reviewed plans and specifications for Phase 1 piping of the Little Wabash Drainage Project and authorized soliciting bids. Discussion included resident feedback concerning downstream flood risks along Little Wabash Creek and potential runoff impacts on watershed water quality.

citizen_concerns.concern: Resident Diane Lathrop submitted an email expressing concern that faster runoff through the new 60-inch storm sewer pipe in the Little Wabash Drainage Project would exacerbate downstream flooding on Lake Road properties and introduce more chemical runoff into Mattoon's water supply watershed.
citizen_concerns.response: The city manager noted that Phase 3 of the drainage project includes planned detention basins behind Bimbo Bakeries and Circle Drive to slow storm runoff, and committed to meeting with the resident to discuss potential project amendments.

action_items.action: Set up a meeting with downstream resident Diane Lathrop to review Little Wabash Drainage Project plans and evaluate potential change orders or design amendments.

votes.measure: Approve $74,868 proposal from Hydro-Kinetics for replacement of modulating electric actuators on Filter #2 at the Water Treatment Plant
